newsitem.title: USA: Rep. Dornan's poll claims disputed.
newsitem.headline: Rep. Dornan's poll claims disputed.

text.p: An Orange County, California, election official Friday disputed a contention by defeated Representative Robert Dornan's lawyer that a recount had turned up hundreds of questionable votes and said there was no sign the poll results would be overturned.

Dornan, a feisty Republican known as "B-1-Bob" because of his strong support for the military, called for the recount after his narrow defeat to political novice Loretta Sanchez in the Nov. 5 election. Dornan blamed voter fraud for his defeat.
Dornan attorney Michael Schroeder alleged that the recount had thus far uncovered about 500 ballots that should be disqualified because of irregularities.

"If the same percentage of irregularities continues throughout the recount, we will have a clear basis to have the election overturned," said Schroeder, who is also vice-chairman of the California Republican Party.
Rosalyn Lever, Orange County's Registrar of Voters, disputed Schroeder's figures. "There is no indication (from the recount thus far) that the election is going to be overturned," Lever told Reuters.
Lever said she did not know where Dornan's attorney got his figures. "I don't know what 500 ballots he was talking about. We haven't seen any evidence of wrongdoing."
In late November, Lever certified that Democratic businesswoman Sanchez, 36, had beaten Dornan, 63, by 984 votes, winning 47,964 votes to his 46,980.

Sanchez spokesman John Shallman said the 500-ballot figure cited by Dornan's attorney was groundless. "They are in a fishing expedition that has proven to be without merit and continues to show Mr. Dornan to be a pathetic cry baby," Shallman said.

"Since the recount has begun, we've increased not decreased the number of votes we are leading by," Shallman added. "Not only are their inquiries proven to be fruitless, but also increasing the margin of victory for Sanchez."
Dornan has alleged non-citizens voted and that ballot boxes were not correctly sealed after the polls.

Of the 500 ballots questioned by Dornan's representatives, Schroeder alleged that two thirds of them were not cast by registered voters, and that about one third should not have been counted because they were submitted by people who were not authorised to submit them.
An estimated 28,000 ballots were expected to be recounted by Friday night, Lever said. The recount should be completed by December 20, she said.
Dornan, a former Air Force pilot, gained a reputation for strong opposition to abortion, communism, homosexual rights and gun control during his 18 years in Congress.
Sanchez, a financial analyst who had never held elected office, campaigned as a moderate while painting Dornan as an extremist out of step with the needs of his largely working-class constituents.
